Subject: SIG/CAIQ: retention of ephemeral session logs and customer carveouts

Hi Jonas —

We're in the middle of a procurement review and our security team has a few SIG/CAIQ questions related to retention and deletion for tenant-scoped logs. Two asks in particular: 1) examples of evidence we can provide to our auditors showing deletion occurred (audit trails, manifests, deletion timestamps), and 2) how Redwood handles customer-specific exceptions/legal-holds for logs (process, SLA to reinstate retention, whether you preserve deleted artifacts for forensics).

Context: we operate with strict data minimization controls and will need an option to request a temporary hold for specific tenant activity during a forensics investigation. Our baseline asks from the auditors: sample retention matrix, a deletion/audit sample, and a short attestation we can include in our SIG mapping. Can Redwood supply these artifacts and a short write-up for CAIQ response items that reference log lifecycle?

Thanks — please loop in whoever owns retention/evidence packaging.

Hannah Li

ClearWave Biosciences

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ: retention of ephemeral session logs and customer carveouts

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a retention matrix, a redacted deletion-audit sample (CSV with timestamps and request IDs), and a one-page attestation for SIG/CAIQ mapping.

High-level retention defaults at Redwood:
- Ephemeral session logs (debug / session-level): default 14 days
- Aggregated request logs / observability traces: 30 days
- Forensics snapshots (customer-requested): retained up to 90 days by default, extendable by contract up to 365 days

Customer-specific legal-hold: we support tenant-scoped holds. Process summary: customer opens a formal retention-hold request via the support portal (or their CSM), we create a hold ticket, and the infra team flags the tenant in the retention control-plane to override TTLs. We keep an immutable audit record (who requested, when, hold id) and produce deletion suspension manifests. After hold release we can provide a certificate of deletion for the held objects once they expire or when customer requests purge.

I'll prepare the three artifacts you asked for and attach the preliminary retention matrix (redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx). Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the SIG mapping and confirm the fields your auditors require?

—Jonas
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Summary of the legal-hold process (short):

2) The hold overrides TTLs for the scoped objects; the infra team sets a hold flag and writes an immutable entry to our audit store.
